name: Edward I completes Welsh conquest
summary: Edward I of England completes the conquest of native Wales with the defeat and death of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (killed November 1282) and the capture and execution of his brother Dafydd (1283). Llywelyn had been the first and last native prince recognized by the English crown (Treaty of Montgomery, 1267); his alliance with Simon de Montfort and his marriage plans (Llywelyn's fiancée Eleanor de Montfort had died in childbirth) created the rift with Edward I. The Statute of Rhuddlan (1284) divides Wales into shires and imposes English law. Edward I's program of castle building (Conwy, Caernarfon, Harlech, Beaumaris) creates the most sophisticated medieval fortification program in Britain.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends native Welsh independence; Edward I's castle-building program is the most systematic in medieval Britain; the Statute of Rhuddlan imposes English administration on Wales; English dominance of Wales is confirmed until the present, no successful Welsh revolt follows
